passages.text: ABSORBENT VESSELS, or LYMPHATICS, in anatomy, a set of thin and transparent vessels which carry a clear fluid called lymph, and which are found in almost every part of the body.
They are furnished with many valves, which give them a knotted appearance; and they unite at last into the thoracic duct, which empties its contents into the left subclavian vein, near the heart.
The lacteals of the intestines, discovered by Asellius in 1622, are of the same kind, and carry the chyle from the food to the blood.
Dr William Hunter and Dr Monro have disputed which of them first showed that these vessels, and not the veins, are the absorbents of the body; and it is now held that the red veins absorb nothing.
In their course the lymphatics pass through the conglobate glands, in which the lymph is thought to be prepared and made more perfect before it enters the blood.
In the scrofula, or king's evil, these glands, chiefly those of the neck, swell and harden, and often break into ulcers that are healed with difficulty.
The lymphatic system is a network of vessels, nodes and organs. Its vessels carry a clear fluid called lymph back towards the heart.

Lymphatic vessels have valves that keep lymph flowing in one direction. Most of the lymph collects in the thoracic duct, which drains into the blood near the junction of the left subclavian and left internal jugular veins.
The lymphatic system returns fluid that leaks from the blood capillaries back to the blood. Most of this fluid, however, is taken back directly into the blood capillaries.
Lacteals in the small intestine absorb fats from digested food.
Lymph passes through lymph nodes, which filter it. The nodes hold large numbers of white blood cells called lymphocytes, which fight infection.
The lymphatic system is part of the immune system.
Lymph nodes often swell during infections. Tuberculosis of the lymph nodes of the neck was formerly called scrofula.
Gaspare Aselli described the lacteals in 1622. Olaus Rudbeck and Thomas Bartholin described the lymphatic vessels of the body in the 1650s.

reasons: Same subject: ABSORBENT VESSELS, or LYMPHATICS and Lymphatic system.
Rare terms appear in both: lymph, thoracic duct, lacteals, scrofula.
Lymph node scores well but covers only the glands.

britannica.quote: thin and transparent vessels which carry a clear fluid called lymph

wikipedia.quote: Its vessels carry a clear fluid called lymph

alignments.label: Valves and the duct

britannica.quote: they unite at last into the thoracic duct, which empties its contents into the left subclavian vein

wikipedia.quote: Most of the lymph collects in the thoracic duct

alignments.note: Same route. Wikipedia gives the joining point of two veins in more detail.

alignments.label: Lacteals, 1622

britannica.quote: The lacteals of the intestines, discovered by Asellius in 1622

wikipedia.quote: Gaspare Aselli described the lacteals in 1622

alignments.note: Same discoverer and year. Asellius is the Latin form of Aselli.

alignments.label: Lacteals carry food

britannica.quote: carry the chyle from the food to the blood

alignments.note: Same function. Today the fat is named, not the chyle.

alignments.label: Only lymphatics absorb

britannica.quote: it is now held that the red veins absorb nothing

wikipedia.quote: Most of this fluid, however, is taken back directly into the blood capillaries

alignments.note: The lymphatics do absorb fluid. But the blood vessels take back most of it, so the claim that veins absorb nothing is wrong.

alignments.label: Glands prepare lymph

britannica.quote: the lymph is thought to be prepared and made more perfect

wikipedia.quote: Lymph passes through lymph nodes, which filter it

alignments.note: The glands are now called lymph nodes. They filter the lymph and hold immune cells; they do not perfect it.

alignments.label: Scrofula

britannica.quote: In the scrofula, or king's evil, these glands, chiefly those of the neck, swell and harden

wikipedia.quote: Tuberculosis of the lymph nodes of the neck was formerly called scrofula

alignments.note: Same disease. Its cause, tuberculosis, was not known in 1797.

wikipedia.quote: white blood cells called lymphocytes, which fight infection

alignments.label: Immune system
alignments.note: The 1797 entry gives the system no role in defence.

suggestedQuestions: Are the lymphatics the only absorbent vessels?
What do the lymph glands do?

Are the lymphatics the only absorbent ve.answer: The 1797 entry says yes: the lymphatics absorb and the red veins absorb nothing [B4]. Wikipedia says the lymphatics return leaked fluid, but most of it goes back directly into the blood capillaries [W3].

What do the lymph glands do?.answer: The 1797 entry thought the glands prepare the lymph and make it more perfect [B5]. Wikipedia says the lymph nodes filter the lymph and hold lymphocytes that fight infection [W5], as part of the immune system [W6].
